subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (Acme)

Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging requirements (Acme)

Hi Samantha / Ben,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. As promised, a short recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points / goals
- PII handling: Acme cannot persist raw customer PII in any long-term storage. Any sensitive tokens or identifiers must be redacted or never stored.
- Auditability: Security and compliance team needs verifiable audit logs for inference requests (who, when, model version) exported to their SIEM.
- Retention windows: Default request logs should be configurable; target is 30 days for detailed logs, with an aggregated/metrics-only retention of 1 year.
- Redaction: Need deterministic redaction at the API ingress (PII redaction and obfuscation rules) and the ability to run post-hoc redaction for historical logs.
- Deployment: Preference for Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for regulated workloads; hosted evaluation OK for POC if data is masked.

Current stack (what you shared)
- Primary apps on AWS (EKS) and S3 for blob storage.
- Existing identity: Okta + SCIM; audit logs routed to Splunk.
- Currently evaluating ways to use LLMs for customer support summarization and routing; high volume of PII in some transcripts.

Success criteria for POC
- No raw PII leaves Acme storage after processing (either redacted client-side or redwood-managed ephemeral-only).
- Audit logs exported to Acme Splunk instance with immutable timestamps and model-version metadata.
- Retention configurable down to 7/30/90 day windows.
- Evidence that redaction works reliably on a 1K-record test set.

Attachments I’m sharing
- redwood-data-privacy-brief.pdf (high-level controls & deployment options)
- redwood-MAP-template.xlsx (mutual action plan template — fill this out with dates and owners)

Next steps
1) I’ll share the MAP and a short technical note on redaction approaches (we protect PII through a combination of client-side masking, in-flight redaction, and optional post-processing).
2) Rishi (cc’d) will follow up with a quick architecture note on audit log exports and KMS/HSM options.
3) Acme to confirm which datasets you want included in the POC and a preferred 1K-record sample for redaction testing.
4) Schedule a follow-up technical call next week (30–45min) to walk the sample flow and confirm export mechanics.

If I missed anything, please flag. Otherwise I’ll assume this captures what we discussed.

Best,

Ben — good questions. Short answers: yes and yes. More detail below and Rishi will add technical specifics.

- Mixed redaction approach: We support client-side masking for POC plus our in-flight server-side redaction. The POC can be run both ways so you can compare recall/precision on the 1K test set. We’ll provide guidance on sample labeling to evaluate.

- Audit log forwarding: Redwood can publish audit events to a customer-managed endpoint. For Splunk we can:
  - Push events to an HTTPS ingest endpoint (if you have a Splunk HEC token) for near-real-time; or
  - Export logs to an S3 bucket (encrypted) on a scheduled basis for batch consumption.

I’ve cc’d Rishi to share the implementation notes (HEC headers, event schema, example CloudWatch/S3 pipeline) and KMS details.

Next for us: Rishi — can you share the brief with the event schema and retention configuration options?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Ben / Samantha — following up with the tech details we discussed. High-level summary first, then specifics you can hand to your infra team.

Summary
- Redaction: We support three redaction tiers: client-side masking (recommended for highest privacy), in-flight deterministic redaction (regex + ML-based named-entity detection), and scheduled post-hoc re-redaction for historical data. For the POC we recommend doing both client-side masking and in-flight redaction so you can measure false positives/negatives.
- Audit logs: Events include request_id, timestamp (RFC3339), model_version, route, latency_ms, token_count, and a hashed user_id (salted per-customer). Payloads do not include raw user content unless explicitly enabled.
- Export options:
  1) Splunk HEC: Redwood can push audit events over HTTPS to your HEC. We support mutual TLS and token-auth. Events are sent near-real-time; batching available for throughput.
  2) S3 export: Encrypted S3 objects delivered on a schedule (hourly/daily). Objects are encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys or Redwood-managed keys depending on deployment.
  3) SIEM streaming via Kafka: for private deployments we can place a Kafka forwarder into your VPC.

Retention & deletion
- Retention windows configurable per-customer and per-data-type. Config options: 7/30/90/365 days.
- Immediate deletion API: We expose an API to trigger deletion of specific request_ids or by time window; operations are logged and return a signed confirmation.

KMS/HSM & key control
- Private deployment: recommended approach is to use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS or on-prem HSM) with envelope encryption. Keys never leave your control.
- Hosted POC: we can use Redwood-managed keys but support bring-your-own KMS for production.

Redaction proofing & evals
- For the 1K-record test we’ll run both masking modes and provide a short report showing recall/precision for detected PII classes (emails, phone numbers, SSNs, account IDs).

Action items for POC setup
- Acme: provide the 1K sample + Splunk HEC endpoint (or S3 bucket IAM role) and identify an infra point-of-contact.
- Redwood (Rishi/Marissa): deliver event schema, HEC example, retention config options, and MAP with dates.

I’ll attach a short event-schema snippet to the MAP we send; Marissa I’ll drop the sample schema into the Drive link you shared.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if your infra team wants to walk through the HEC integration.

— Rishi Malhotra
